rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 15 mm apart across x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, placed 60 mm ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. The 12 mm footprint is about half the tape width, which gives a smooth reading as the tape moves under the array, and the 60 mm total span keeps the outer sensors off the tape until the robot is well off line. Controller: antisymmetric weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] make the signal a direct left/right error estimate. kp = 2.5 gives a moderate steering response, kd = 0.3 damps the swing on bends, and ki = 0 avoids integral windup on the curves. base_speed = 1.4 targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s, with some margin for bends. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning the way it was heading when the tape is lost. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with low rms_error. Risks: speed may be too high for the tighter slalom bends, which would show as line-loss events or off-track exits. Hypotheses to test next: (1) lowering base_speed slightly reduces max_error on the slalom; (2) raising kd reduces steering_oscillation; (3) the completion_time at base_speed 1.4 is under 3 s with margin. Measurements requested: all, to see the speed/accuracy trade-off.
